Welcome to Seva Education
Seva Education provides a school setting for students with learning disabilities. The majority of our pupils and students have a diagnosis of Autistic Spectrum Condition (ASC) with a significant number also experiencing Speech, Language & Communication (SLCN) difficulties, Social Emotional & Mental Health (SEMH) challenges and other complex needs. We offer a range of settings across London and Hertfordshire for students with an EHCP between the ages of 5 and 25.
Vision
Our vision is for helping every child achieve their best. Through great teaching, nurturing support and enriching experiences, we build confidence, independence and resilience – so pupils leave us ready for the next stage of their education.
Testimonials
Seva Education in Harrow has an incredible school family! The teachers, staff and admin are invested in supporting the students. It is apparent that kids feel seen, included and cared about here.
Thanks to all the teachers at Seva Education. You are doing a wonderful job.
I enjoy working at Seva Education, everyone goes above and beyond. The team keeps us going and together so we can get good results.
To be a part of such a great team brings me joy and allows my work day to be filled with happiness. The staff have a passion for our student’s progression and I am thankful to be a part of this team.
Staff feel well supported by leaders and like working at the school. They say that workload is not a problem and that leaders consider their well-being. Staff are enthusiastic and motivated. They work hard, with students’ best interests at heart.
Pupils like coming to this school. They are happy, and they feel safe. Each one of the three school sites is a welcoming environment. Pupils have a chance to get out in the fresh air by going to different places like local parks, cafes and shops.
Our philosophy
At Seva, we believe children thrive when they feel known, valued and challenged. We promote positive relationships, strong routines and a love of learning – working in partnership with parents and carers every step of the way.

Personal Development
At Seva Education, personal development is at the heart of everything we do. Our values and ethos underpin everyday life within our school community and support each pupil and student to become confident, respectful, independent, and active members of society. We are committed to ensuring that every individual is prepared for adulthood through meaningful experiences that promote wellbeing, resilience, communication, independence, and positive relationships.
Our personal development offer is designed to meet the diverse needs of pupils and students within a SEND environment. Through a personalised and inclusive approach, we support learners to develop the knowledge, skills, confidence, and cultural understanding needed to live healthy, safe, and fulfilling lives. Every lesson and experience provides an opportunity to connect learning to the wider world in ways that are engaging, relevant, and accessible.
The promotion of British Values is central to our curriculum and school culture. Pupils and students are taught the importance of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect, and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs. These principles are embedded throughout school life and are reflected in our core values of Equality, Aspiration, Respect, and Humanity. We actively encourage learners to express their views, listen to others, and understand the importance of fairness, responsibility, and inclusion.
Social, Moral, Spiritual and Cultural (SMSC) development is woven throughout the curriculum and wider school experiences. Through Religion and Worldviews, PSHE/RSE, enrichment activities, assemblies, tutor sessions, and themed learning days, pupils and students explore different cultures, communities, beliefs, and perspectives. They are supported to understand themselves and others, celebrate diversity, and develop respect for people from all backgrounds and experiences.
Our PSHE/RSE curriculum empowers pupils and students with the knowledge and confidence to make informed choices about their health, wellbeing, safety, relationships, and future aspirations. Learning is carefully adapted to meet individual needs and developmental stages, ensuring that all pupils and students can access and benefit from the curriculum in a meaningful way. We promote healthy lifestyles through learning about emotional wellbeing, physical health, online safety, healthy relationships, and understanding where food comes from, including opportunities for practical outdoor learning and horticulture.
At Seva Education, we recognise the importance of pupil voice and active participation. Pupils and students are encouraged to contribute to school life through opportunities such as School Council, restorative conversations, enrichment activities, and community engagement. These experiences help learners develop confidence, communication skills, independence, and a sense of responsibility towards others.
We are committed to creating a safe, nurturing, and inclusive environment where individuality is celebrated and all forms of discrimination, bullying, or prejudice are challenged. Through consistent support and positive relationships, pupils and students learn to value themselves and others, develop self-esteem, and build the skills needed to succeed in further education, employment, and adult life.
The impact of our personal development curriculum is seen in pupils and students who are increasingly confident, resilient, reflective, and prepared for the next stage of their lives. They leave Seva Education with the ability to make informed decisions, engage positively with their communities, and contribute meaningfully to society.

Student Careers Advice
Careers Guidance at Seva Education
At Seva Education, we deliver a careers programme which builds on our learners’ unique strengths, raises their aspirations, and provides access to information & opportunities to achieve their potential and thrive in the wider community.
We take a whole school approach to careers with embedded learning though individual subjects, PSHE and Life Skills lessons which provide students with a clear understanding of how their learning relates to both the wider and professional world. Through a personalised curriculum, pupils have the opportunity to build a portfolio of skills they can evidence for use in future applications.
With the support of trained, independent personal advisors, inhouse guidance and the engagement of external providers, our careers programme ensures students are able to make well-informed decisions based on both technical and academic options.
The Gatsby Benchmarks set out a framework for schools to deliver ‘good career guidance’ and serve as the foundation of the careers programme we offer at Seva Education.
1. A stable careers programme
We use Compass Plus to track and build on our careers provision.
2. Learning from career and labour market
3. Addressing the needs of each pupil
Careers guidance which explores market information and future opportunities tailored to individual interest areas.
4. Linking curriculum learning to careers
Embedded in curriculum learning and delivered through the PSHE/ Life Skills curriculum, the Talentino Careers at Every Level Programme, assemblies and drop-down days.
5. Encounters with employers and employees
Met through careers talks by employers virtual programmes.
6. Experiences of workplaces
We work in collaboration with families to secure opportunities and facilitate virtual work experience opportunities.
7. Encounters with further and higher education
8. Personal guidance
Connexions advisors visit to offer independent careers advice in addition to inhouse guidance.
Careers Advice
We believe that all of our students should have access to relevant careers advice. We achieve this through the following:
Visits from employers
Visits from specialist careers advisors (Connexions)
Information from local authorities and charities
Work Experience
All of our students have the right to explore and gain experience of the work environment. This will look different for each student depending on their needs.
We are now using the Compass+ tool, so we can benchmark, manage, track and evaluate our school’s careers provision at an individual student level against the Gatsby Benchmarks. This aim is to ensure our careers provision is continually improving and adapting to be the best it can be, giving consideration to the changing landscape of careers and local market information.
*For more information about our programme or to request access as a provider please contact either Gavin Winters, or Anna Vermond, via the school office.

Remote Learning
At Seva Education, we believe that learning should never stand still. Whether our pupils and students are walking through our school doors or engaging from home, our mission remains the same: to provide an ambitious, supportive, and engaging education tailored to every child’s needs.
Our Blended Learning approach ensures that even when students cannot be physically on-site, they remain connected to their teachers, and their progress. While nothing can truly replace the magic of face-to-face interaction, our flexible remote provision ensures that no child is left behind.
Our Blended Learning Philosophy
Above all, we aim to keep our students excited about learning. We focus on three core pillars to ensure sustainability and success:
Wellbeing: Prioritising mental health and social connection.
A Comprehensive Curriculum, Delivered Digitally
We continue to deliver vital interventions remotely, including Phonics, Reading/Writing support, English and Maths.
The Power of Microsoft Teams
We have designed our digital platform in collaboration with parents and teachers to be as user-friendly as possible.
Our Guarantee to Families
In the event of a student being on Blended Learning, remote learning will usually commence the very next working day. Every Seva Education site commits to:
Our Commitments to You
On certain occasions, we may also provide bespoke physical learning packs to ensure the approach is perfectly tailored to the individual student’s needs. At our college site a personalised approach is used.
Together, we ensure that pupils and students continue to grow, learn, and flourish—wherever they are.

Curriculum
Our Curriculum Supports Students’ Individual Needs
Our Curriculum
Intent
Our curriculum is broad and balanced and uses the Cornerstones Scheme of Work as the starting point, differentiated to meet the needs of students. Students are placed on one of the pathways based on the needs outlined in their EHCPs, reports from professionals and in school assessments. The school then uses baseline assessments and diagnostic reports to ensure that the curriculum matches their needs.
In previous settings our students may not have been successful in their learning, possibly because they have missed time in lessons or school altogether. In many cases, knowledge and skills may have been taught but due to students special needs not being identified early enough, they were not given the opportunity to ensure that it was transferred into their long term memories so that they could access it for future use. Our curriculum is designed to introduce new knowledge and skills and to fill the gaps from previously missed learning opportunities.
The intent for our curriculum is therefore threefold:
We know that, based on their past experiences in schools, information from EHCPs and the detailed reports from professionals, our students will have barriers to learning the curriculum content they need for success. Our curriculum is designed to overcome these barriers so that students can achieve the educational goals we share for them.
Our curriculum is designed to be:
Broad and balanced curriculum
Teaches a wide range of topics
Curriculum Implementation
We uses a number of well tested schemes of work to enable teachers to deliver lessons and content that meets the needs of our students.
Reading and Phonics
The school uses Read, Write, Inc to teach phonics and reading to students.
Introduction
Read Write Inc. is a comprehensive literacy program developed by Ruth Miskin, aimed at helping students learn to read and write fluently. It is particularly focused on early years and primary education, designed to create a solid foundation in phonics, comprehension, writing, and spelling.
The programme is designed for students aged 4-7. However, at Seva Education we will continue teaching READ, WRITE, INC to students beyond the age of 7 as many of our students have not learned to read when they join us due to adverse experiences in previous settings.
Read, Write, Inc was developed by Ruth Miskin and more information on this can be found here.
Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education (PSHE)
This scheme of work draws on planning and guidance from the PSHE Association, as recommended by the DfE.
Mathematics
At Seva Education we often need to place students in mixed age classes matched to need and/or ability. Whilst we try to place students in similar ability classes this is not always possible as a reading ability may be very different from a mathematical ability or social and emotional level of maturity.
In order to meet the needs of all students we teach using the White Rose scheme of work which allows teachers to teach concepts to mixed ability groups initially students can then also be supported by other adults in and out of class through the wide range of resources that are available in the White Rose scheme.
Students can be supported though the following resources:
Long term overviews
Individual lesson plans
Whiteboard lessons plans
Videos to explain mathematical thinking
End of block and term assessments
Foundation Subjects
The school uses Curriculum Maestro for foundation planning and recording student assessment data. Curriculum Maestro gives users access to the Cornerstones Curriculum planning tool which is used for all foundation subjects. Foundation subjects are taught on a rolling two-year basis so that students do not repeat topics as they move through the school. The themes or topics are also planned to meet the needs of mixed age groups in classes and also to pathway that a student is placed on.

English as an Additional Language
Intent
At Seva Education, we recognise that a pupil’s EAL (English as an Additional Language) status is determined by the language first learned and spoken at home. We are proud of our diverse and inclusive community, where all cultures, languages, and backgrounds are valued and celebrated. Every child is welcomed, respected, and supported to achieve their full potential.
We are committed to ensuring that the teaching, learning, achievement, attitudes, and wellbeing of all pupils are fully supported. Our curriculum reflects and celebrates the rich cultural experiences and backgrounds of our learners, recognising the importance of each child’s cultural capital. Through our diverse, text-led curriculum, we provide meaningful learning opportunities that build upon pupils’ prior experiences, languages, and identities.
As a school, we understand the distinction between social communication skills and academic language proficiency. We recognise that some pupils may be able to access and understand the curriculum at a higher level than their spoken English may initially suggest. Our provision is therefore carefully tailored to ensure that language is never a barrier to learning, participation, or achievement.
The aim of this policy is to ensure that we meet the full range of needs of pupils learning English as an additional language, in line with the requirements of the Equality Act 2010. We are committed to working in partnership with families and use platforms such as the ClassDojo to support effective communication through translation features, enabling greater parental engagement and accessibility.
Implementation
What is our EAL provision at Seva Education?
Early English language skills are identified and supported through careful assessment processes, including diagnostic and observational tools. These assessments enable staff to monitor individual pupils’ development and identify strengths and areas for support in the following areas:
Seva Education recognises that pupils with EAL who require additional language support do not automatically have SEND needs. Equally, we recognise that some EAL pupils may also have SEND needs, and where identified, they will have full and equitable access to the school’s SEND provision. We also acknowledge that pupils learning English as an additional language may demonstrate high levels of ability, giftedness, or talent, even if they are not yet fully fluent in English.
We are committed to providing high-quality professional development for staff to strengthen their understanding of effective EAL pedagogy and inclusive teaching practices. Staff training and resources, including support from Learning Village, help ensure that teaching strategies are responsive to the needs of EAL learners.
All staff actively support pupils learning English as an additional language through a range of inclusive strategies, including:
Language acquisition
Social interaction and communication
Developing spoken, understood, and written English by:
Ensuring access to the curriculum and assessment by:
At Seva Education, we follow a structured and supportive induction process for new EAL learners to ensure that pupils settle quickly, feel welcomed, and are able to access learning from the earliest opportunity.
Impact
How do we monitor this?
At Seva Education, we strive to ensure that every pupil, regardless of their level of English proficiency, can access learning alongside their peers and participate fully in school life. Pupils and their families are supported to develop confidence and competence in English while maintaining and valuing their home language and cultural identity.
Staff maintain high expectations for all pupils with EAL and monitor progress carefully through both formative and summative assessment. EAL pupils are regularly discussed during Pupil Progress meetings, where staff collaborate to share effective practice, review provision, and identify any additional support needs at the earliest opportunity.
Through our inclusive approach, pupils receiving EAL support make progress academically, socially, and emotionally. They develop the communication skills, confidence, and independence needed to access the curriculum, engage positively within the school community, and prepare successfully for the next stages of education and adult life.

Work Experience
Work Experience & Employment
Work experience is a crucial way to develop key skills and self-confidence. At Seva Education we provide equal opportunities and ‘learning for all’ to develop a wide range of life skills that can be achieved through our work experience pathways. Work experience starts from Year 10 onwards for our students.
We raise aspirations and ensure our students have the opportunity to develop the life skills which will allow them to become as independent as possible, so they can access the wider community and world of work.
School Work Experience (15–16 Year olds)
As part of the Preparation for Adulthood (PfA) pathways, one of the key components for developing independence is Employment. We ensure that our students at Seva Education obtain the appropriate skills across the board, which will support their transition to adulthood.
The core elements of employment are embedded across the curriculum through practical, real-world learning and structured work experience opportunities. This ensures students can apply what they have learned in meaningful contexts and build confidence in workplace environments before progressing into placements.
Further Education Work Experience (17–25 Year olds)
Seva Education has designed a solid foundation for young people with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) as they transition to work and independent living.
Our FE college offers a supported work experience programme in partnership with Hilton Wembley. This provides students with regular, structured access to a professional hotel environment, where they develop workplace behaviours, follow routines, and build confidence alongside industry staff. We also have our own allotment sites and provide our learners with opportunities to learn about horticulture, increasing employability skills for those seeking a career in related professions.
